knowledge:
- key_parameters: viewpoint=Genomic coordinate of the 4C-seq viewpoint ;; viewpointChromosome=Chromosome of the viewpoint (e.g., "chr10") ;; distance=Genomic distance from the viewpoint to filter fragment data during import ;; maxSQSigma=Maximum square sigma for scale-space and fingerprint map calculation ;; plotIP=Logical, whether to plot matching inflection points in plotInflectionPoints ;; guessViewpoint=Logical, if TRUE, automatically matches remaining contours at lower sigma assuming they belong to peaks ;; useLog=Logical, whether to use log2 transformation of sigma in outputScaleSpaceTree
- alternatives: Basic4Cseq=Used for initial 4C-seq pipeline processing; Scale4C specifically imports Basic4Cseq's fragment-based table output to perform scale-space analysis.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you want to qualitatively describe a 4C-seq signal, track genomic features (peaks and valleys) across multiple smoothing scales, and visualize the structural complexity and stability of genomic interactions via 2D tesselation maps.
- pitfalls: Singularities can be missed at high sigma values where contours are stretched and holes appear in the fingerprint map ;; Singularities can be marked erroneously multiple times for large, frazzled contours, requiring manual deletion or adjustment of epsilon ;; Sigma = 1 is difficult to trace due to high density of inflection point curves and false singularities ;; Tracking lines may not match the inflection point curves correctly, requiring manual correction of coordinates in the singularities GRanges object.

workflows.name: scale_space_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform scale-space transformation, singularity tracking, manual correction, and tesselation visualization on 4C-seq fragment data.
input: liverData.csv (Basic4Cseq fragment-based table output containing raw 4C-seq reads)
vp.txt (tab-separated text file containing points of interest/viewpoint coordinates)
workflows.stages: 1. Import raw fragment data using importBasic4CseqData ;; 2. Initialize the Scale4C object using Scale4C ;; 3. Add points of interest using addPointsOfInterest and pointsOfInterest<- ;; 4. Plot inflection points for specific sigma values using plotInflectionPoints ;; 5. Calculate the scale-space matrix using calculateScaleSpace ;; 6. Compute the fingerprint map using calculateFingerprintMap ;; 7. Identify and track singularities using findSingularities ;; 8. Manually correct or add singularities (e.g., viewpoint singularity) in the GRanges object ;; 9. Plot the final tesselation map using plotTesselation ;; 10. Export the scale-space tree structure using outputScaleSpaceTree
workflows.code:
csvFile <- system.file("extdata", "liverData.csv", package="Scale4C")
liverReads <- importBasic4CseqData(csvFile, viewpoint = 21160072, 
    viewpointChromosome = "chr10", distance = 1000000)
liverData = Scale4C(rawData = liverReads, viewpoint = 21160072, viewpointChromosome = "chr10")
poiFile <- system.file("extdata", "vp.txt", package="Scale4C")
pointsOfInterest(liverData) <- addPointsOfInterest(liverData, 
    read.csv(poiFile, sep = "\t", stringsAsFactor = FALSE))
plotInflectionPoints(liverData, 2, fileName = "", plotIP = FALSE)
plotInflectionPoints(liverData, 50, fileName = "", plotIP = FALSE)
scaleSpace(liverData) = calculateScaleSpace(liverData, maxSQSigma = 10)
liverData = calculateFingerprintMap(liverData, maxSQSigma = 10)
singularities(liverData) = findSingularities(liverData, 1, guessViewpoint = FALSE)
data(liverData)
singularities(liverData) = c(singularities(liverData), GRanges("chr10", IRanges(39, 42),
    "*", "sqsigma" = 2000, "left" = 40, "right" = 41, "type" = "peak"))
tempSingularities = singularities(liverData)
tempSingularities$left[30] = 235
tempSingularities$right[30] = 250
tempSingularities$type[30] = "peak"
singularities(liverData) = tempSingularities
data(liverDataVP)
plotTesselation(liverDataVP, fileName = "")
outputScaleSpaceTree(liverDataVP, useLog = FALSE)
